svg.title: Electrically controlled 2×2 Mach–Zehnder optical switch
svg.desc: Editable, annotation-free top-down functional symbol for a two-input, two-output Mach–Zehnder optical switch. Two distinct waveguides approach in a nominal balanced directional coupler, separate into equal-length interferometer arms, approach in a second nominal balanced directional coupler, then separate into two outputs. There are no Y junctions or crossings. A gold electrode and electrical control terminal represent differential phase control on the upper arm; the electrical return and any static bias elements are omitted. Calibrated differential phase selects the bar or cross routing state; a pi change exchanges the two outputs. Route phases must be calibrated when the switch carries coherent signals. Both optical outputs are retained. This is a functional schematic, not a fabrication layout: coupling length, waveguide spacing, bends, actuator technology, operating wavelength, optical bandwidth, extinction and switching time are unspecified. Short leads, continuous pale gray cladding and blue cores match the component library. There are no fiber outlines, enclosing box, visible labels or background. All artwork is native vector SVG with separate editable layers. Optical port centers: upper input (16,48), lower input (16,112), upper output (384,48), lower output (384,112). Electrical terminal center: (200,13). Directional coupling regions occupy x=66 to 98 and x=302 to 334, with guide centers at y=70 and y=90.
